name: CR-Int-14-substitution-3.b
questiontext:
Evaluate the following definite integral: \[\int^{{CT:0}}_{{CT:1}} {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}}\] Hint: Use the substitution \(u = {{CT:4}}\)
[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]
generalfeedback:
We need to solve \[\int {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}}\] using the substitution \(u = {{CT:4}}\) <hint>calc_int_methods_substitution</hint>.

So, if \(u = {{CT:4}}\), then \({{CT:3}} = {{CT:5}}\) and \(d{{CT:3}} = {{CT:6}}d{{CT:7}}\).

Hence,

\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle
\int {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  \int [{{CT:8}}] {{CT:6}}d{{CT:7}} \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  \int [{{CT:9}} d{{CT:7}} \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:10}}+c \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:11}}+c
 \end{array}\]

We need \[\int^{{CT:0}}_{{CT:1}} {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}} \]
so, recall that if \[\int f(x) dx = F(x)+c\] then \[\int^a_b f(x) dx = F(a) - F(b).\]

So, let \[F({{CT:3}}) = {{CT:11}}\]

Then,

\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle
\int^{{CT:0}}_{{CT:1}} {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  F({{CT:0}}) - F({{CT:1}}) \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:12}}-{{CT:13}} \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:14}}
 \end{array}\]

on_true.feedback: This is a definite integration problem, so your answer should be a number.  This is the correct integral, but you have not evaluated it.
